sections.h2: Why is Lee County property tax different for a Leesburg-area seller?
sections.html:
Lee is the priciest of the four Georgia counties in this research set, and its tax pages show a county that has grown quickly. Leesburg holds both offices, so most paperwork for a sale starts there.

QuickFacts, the Census Bureau's comparison table, shows Lee gaining from 28,298 people in 2010 to an estimated 34,179 in mid-2025, on 355.88 square miles of land. Lee owners hold 74.2 percent of its 13,411 housing units, and the middle home is valued at $231,800. Median household income is $89,168, the highest of the four. About 34.1 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 65.5 percent of residents 16 and up are in the labor force.

Leesburg-area workers spend 23.1 minutes getting to a job, and poverty sits at 9.7 percent. Building crews pulled 94 permits in 2025. Buyers with that kind of income will read a tax bill closely, so have the latest copy ready.

sections.h2: What are monthly housing costs in Lee County?
sections.html:
Costs run above the neighboring counties. The 2020 to 2024 Census tallies show Lee owners paying a median $1,605 a month with a mortgage and $532 without, against $1,184 for renters.

  • 12,287 households live here, averaging 2.66 people.
  • 96.0 percent have a computer and 90.7 percent a broadband subscription.
  • About 88.1 percent of residents stayed in the same house for a year.
  • Retail sales were near $323.0 million in 2022.

Most Lee owners stay put, so a seller who documents taxes and exemptions stands out. Bring the last bill, the deed and any exemption letter to the first meeting with your closing attorney.

sections.h2: Which Leesburg offices handle a Lee County bill and a value?
sections.html:
Both offices are in Leesburg. Lee's own tax site stresses that the commissioner neither sets values nor sets rates.

A county assessors page says three board members serve three year terms by appointment of the county commissioners, and the board picks the chief appraiser. The board meets on the second Monday of each month at 4:30 p.m. in the Leslie Highway office, and the page links to online property records and a request form for withholding records from public view.

sections.h2: When do Lee County bills come due, and how do payments count?
sections.html:
December 20 is the general due date on Lee's tax site. A mailed payment counts on a USPS postmark, and a postage meter stamp does not, so mail early.

Interest and penalties after that date follow O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 and 48-2-44. Lee's site cautions that a parcel left unpaid can be levied upon and sold. Payments can also be made online.

A recent episode matters to anyone who bought in 2025. Lee issued refund checks for tax year 2025 solely to the owner of record on January 1, 2025, with none sent to mortgage or escrow companies:

  • Buyers who closed afterward should check closing papers for any share.
  • Lee's commissioner will not divide a check between the two parties.
  • Escrow customers can ask the assessors for a letter to send their servicer.

The county site adds that the Board of Commissioners chose to issue refund checks in place of crediting future bills, and that any complaint about that choice belongs with your county commissioner. Because the check went to the person, not the lender, an owner whose escrow account paid the 2025 bill must pass the money to the mortgage company so it can be credited back.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Lee County value?
sections.html:
Lee appraisers look at recent sales and conditions on January 1, and notices usually go out in spring. Appeal in writing to the board within 45 days of the notice date, and say how you want it heard.

The case can go to the Board of Equalization and then Superior Court, or to arbitration. Lee's site says the appeal cannot be about the amount of tax levied. Returns go to the board from January 1 through April 1. Standing timber is taxed only when sold or cut, at 100 percent of market value. For value questions, ring 229-759-6010.

sections.h2: Which Lee County exemptions can I claim or pass along?
sections.html:
Lee adds local exemptions to the state set, and whichever amount is larger controls. The application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, due April 1.

  • First-time owners bring a copy of the warranty deed.
  • Your driver's license has to show a physical Lee County address, because a post office box is refused.
  • Once granted, it carries forward until you change residence or ownership.

The county's tax page prints the whole menu, from the $2,000 standard exemption through elderly school and general exemptions, disabled veteran relief, a floating exemption and a deferral program. Read it with the income limits it states. Brownfield sites can have their value frozen for a decade, and manufacturers apply for Freeport before April 1.

sections.h2: Who owes the Lee County tax in the year I sell?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner, because no part-year refund exists in Georgia. Your closing attorney divides the bill.

  • Phone 229-759-6015 to see whether this year's bill is out and paid.
  • Request a payoff for any open balance.
  • Tell the buyer to file a fresh homestead application, because yours ends with your ownership.

If timber stood on your land, file the county's timber sale or harvest report, which both office pages link to.

sections.h2: What do Lee County residents look like on paper?
sections.html:
Children under 5 are 5.0 percent of Lee's population and children under 18 another 22.7 percent, while 16.9 percent of residents are 65 or older. The Census counts 2,560 veterans, 4.3 percent foreign-born residents and 5.4 percent who speak another language at home. Some 92.4 percent of adults finished high school.

Health care and social assistance receipts were about $41.4 million in 2022, far below Laurens and Liberty. Total employment grew 5.2 percent from 2022 to 2023 across 440 employers, with a payroll near $198.7 million, and 3,324 firms have no employees. The 2020 census counted 33,163 residents, so the county has added roughly a thousand people since.

sections.h2: How do I file a Lee County property tax return?
sections.html:
File with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1, the same window as the homestead deadline. A real property return renews each year at the value set the year before, so a second filing is needed only after you add property, build or want to declare a new figure. Personal property returns must be refiled every year.

Owners who disagree with the board's number can declare a different one on a new return, which opens the appeal process if the board does not accept it. Call the assessors at 229-759-6010 for forms.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Lee County tax bill?
faqs.a: At the commissioner's office, 100 Starksville Avenue North in Leesburg, by mail to P.O. Box 9, or online on the Lee tax site.

faqs.q: Does a postage meter stamp count on a Lee payment?
faqs.a: No. Lee accepts a United States Postal Service postmark only. Mail early or pay online.

faqs.q: Who received the Lee County 2025 refund check on a house that sold?
faqs.a: The owner of record on January 1, 2025. The commissioner does not split checks, so buyer and seller settle it themselves.

faqs.q: What do first-time Lee homeowners bring to file a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: A copy of the warranty deed and a driver's license showing the Lee County address.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Lee value only because my tax rose?
faqs.a: No. The appeal must rest on taxability, value or uniformity, or a denied exemption, filed within 45 days of the notice.
